IAMA a dude who grew up in Wheeling, WV. AMA

You mean in the actual town? In the woods outside? Do you have any perspective from seeing other parts of the country that makes you think Wheeling is unique? For example, someone who grew up in suburban Pittsburgh or pretty much anywhere in Ohio, may be about the same thing. What about Wheeling makes an AMA?

In the actual town, but kind of out of the way in the Bethlehem area.

Wheeling is locked 10 years behind the rest of the country. Driving across the Fort Henry Bridge is kinda like this.

Wheeling is a much smaller town than Pittsburgh, even though they are close. Worse economy for sure. The only thing residents have in common with suburban Pittsburgh is the use of the word "yens" (which means "ya'll").

Wheeling makes a good AMA topic because nobody knows shit about it. I'm not saying they should, mind.

EDIT: This is the crappy little house I lived in.
In Pittsburgh, it's pronounced "yinz" for the record. Sorry, Pittsburgh native here. I get...touchy regarding stuff about my hometown. Perhaps I should do my own AMA?

Dude, I love going to the Cabela's down there. They used to have this enormous catfish that just laid on a rock and gasped like a 800lb man that just took his first steps in 5 years.

I'm about an hour north of Pittsburgh, I used to work right where PA, OH, and WV meet but in PA. We're pretty close.

They were putting that in around the time I moved away. The area is called the Highlands. They got a ton of chains (Target, Panera, Quaker Steak & Lube, etc.) that had never been seen before in the area.

They claimed the Highlands would save the area, but the last time I was back all anybody talked about was the heroin epidemic.
From Pittsburgh here. I remember going to Wheeling, WV once with my mom when I was young. All I remember is the awesome chili-dog I had while there.

Louis's Hot Dogs! They were in downtown Wheeling, then moved out to Elm Grove when I was 17 or so.

My mom told me that in the 70s the Hare Krishnas would do dances and sell flowers on the plaza by Louis's. The Krishnas have a temple called the Palace of Gold out in the boonies. I never made it out there.

Hey all. Long-term reddit user (got my 9-year badge, can you believe it???), very much disappointed by the direction they're currently taking... I hope voat becomes the new front page of the internet. ;)

You'll probably see me hanging around /v/rpg, if that's your thing.
Stuff like /v/rpg is very much my thing. What's you're favorite pen and paper system?

Huh. You want a full list? :P

Currently I'm leaning mostly towards rules-light and/or narrative systems. When I do play (I rarely do :( ) I run Savage Worlds games in various settings, I find it's not too rules-heavy while not being too open-ended (this seems to scare off potentials players). I've also ran Dungeon World with great success. I love Fate and played a few times on Roll20. I also love anything cyberpunk that fits the rules-light/narrative conditions (sorry Shadowrun!). My next project would be a campaign using the Jaws of the Six Serpents rules or finally launching a Spears of the Dawn campaign or a Barebones Fantasy one. Ugh. So many games, so little players and so little time! What a tragedy.

What about yours?

I know it's a little cliché, but I tend to enjoy Pathfinder, 5th ed., Shadowrun depending on the DM, and I've always wanted to try the Warhammer family of RPGs. I confess, I haven't really had the opportunity to try the more open-ended, story driven stuff, but I'd love to try them someday.

 

I've always been attracted to the combat and puzzle solving aspects of RPGs, so I got into war/board games; especially the skirmish level stuff. Warmahordes and Infinity are at the top of my list at the moment, and I really want to give 40k a shot.

 

As far as the cyberpunk stuff goes, if you ever need people for a game, a friend of mine and I might be able to help you out. He's an absolute nut for anything cyberpunk, and I'm certainly into it as well.

Why is it cliché? You enjoy what you enjoy and that's it. :) But if someday you want to try the narrative way, do check out Dungeon World, it's free if you weren't aware of that. Awesome game and very easy to pick up for D&D players.

If I start an online cyberpunk game I'll be sure to notify you. :) In fact I'll probably start an online game by the end of the summer but probably not anything cyberpunk yet, as I mentioned I'm eyeing SotD and BBF. Stay tuned and watch /v/lfg !
I'll certainly check out Dungeon World, and I've heard a lot of good things about Savage Worlds.

SW strikes a good balance between rules and simplicity: I'd call it "rules-medium". The nice thing about it is that's a truckload of setting for SW in any genre you can imagine: fantasy, sci-fi, cyberpunk, pulp, historical, horror, you name it, there's one (and likely much more than one). Plus the basic book's only ten bucks.

As for DW it's a great gateway since it's very similar (on the surface) to D&D. On my first game I GM'ed I distributed character sheets to my players and had to leave for 10-15 minutes: when I came back, everyone was about halfway through character creation. It's that simple, really, and it feels familiar (same classes, 6 stats in the 3-18 range, etc.)
